transcript: Speaker A: Mom? What is this? Speaker B: Michael... this is Jason. Speaker C: Nice to meet you. Speaker A: Wait... you're on a date? Speaker B: Yes. Is that a problem? Speaker A: Mom, he looks much younger than you. Speaker B: I know that. Speaker A: This feels strange. Speaker C: I understand why you're surprised. Speaker A: Mom, why didn't you tell me? Speaker B: Because I knew you would react like this. Speaker A: I'm just worried about you. Speaker B: Worried... or embarrassed? Speaker A: That's not fair. Speaker B: For many years, I lived only for my family. Speaker A: And we appreciate that. Speaker B: But now I want to enjoy my own life too. Speaker C: Your mom is funny, smart, and kind. Speaker A: You really like spending time with her? Speaker C: Yes. We talk for hours. She makes me happy. Speaker A: Mom... are you happy? Speaker B: Honestly? Yes, I am. Speaker A: I just don't want anyone to hurt you. Speaker B: I know. But being lonely hurts too. Speaker A: I never thought about that. Speaker B: I'm still a person, Michael. I still want friendship, laughter, and happiness. Speaker C: I care about her very much. Speaker A: Maybe I judged too quickly. Speaker B: That's all I wanted you to understand. Speaker A: I'm sorry, Mom. Speaker C: Thank you. So... can we all sit down now? Speaker A: Yeah. I think we can try.
